title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It reduces the dimensionality of the data while preserving as much variance as possible.

title: First Principal Component
text: The first principal component is the direction in which the data varies the most. It is the line that minimizes the squared distance to all the data points.

title: Reconstruction Error
text: Reconstruction error is the difference between the original data and the data reconstructed from the principal components. Using more principal components generally reduces the reconstruction error.
